objective: A live-decision page must materially reduce a real trip decision beyond what a search snippet or the official source already provides. Search traffic is an outcome; decision surplus is the product gate.

fiveSecondAnswer.pass: The primary decision is understandable in under five seconds on a phone.

actionTranslation.pass: The result says what changes in the visitor's plan, not only what the source says.

multiSignalSynthesis.pass: The tool combines the signals that actually control the decision, or explains why one authoritative source is sufficient.

evidenceAndFreshness.pass: Source, observation time, refresh time and truthful degraded state are visible.

temporalContext.pass: The user can tell whether the answer applies now, later today, tomorrow, or only seasonally.

spatialSpecificity.pass: The answer resolves the relevant route, ramp, entrance, viewing area or segment instead of a vague destination-wide state.

fallbackOrAlternative.pass: A bad or ambiguous state gives a useful next move: reroute, choose another area, wait, or verify a named source.

repeatUtility.pass: There is a reason to return when conditions change.

mobileScanability.pass: Verdict, consequence and next check fit the first mobile interaction without card hunting.

failureHonesty.pass: Missing or ambiguous upstream data never becomes a reassuring answer.

lossFunction.definition: Decision loss measures how much work or uncertainty remains after using the page. Lower is better.
lossFunction.target: Loss <= 15 for a breakout-ready tool; loss <= 30 for a useful decision tool.

hardVetoes: The page merely repeats one official open/closed line with no material decision surplus.
A green or positive state could be mistaken for a safety all-clear when another controlling signal is missing.
The live source cannot be verified or truthfully degraded when unavailable.
The primary search intent is already owned by another Chris Izworski canonical.
The page needs thin doorway variants to create demand.

baselineBeforeValuePass.largestGap: No trend/forecast context; route consequence needed closer to the live verdict.
Good synthesis, but the user still has to translate forecast wording into an alarm-clock decision.
Ramp rows are data-heavy; strongest current launch candidates are not prioritized.
Multiple access gates are useful, but the page does not yet turn them into a rim-choice workflow.
Forecast + access is useful, but the consequence and flip conditions are buried.
Elevation is not enough; named launch-site choice remains too dependent on the official page.
Official NPS status already answers much of the query; through-travel consequence must be explicit.
The current page is close to a one-line NPS mirror; detour consequence is the missing product value.
A park-wide text classifier cannot replace the official segment map for a route-network decision.
Area-specific approach roads matter more than a park-wide open/closed read.

implementedValuePass.change: Current result is followed by trip consequence, flip conditions and a pre-commit checklist.
Adds a full-crossing workbench separating west-side extent, Logan Pass/alpine status, east-side extent and vehicle-size gate.
Uses the named NPS launch table, supports motorized versus paddle/small-craft decisions, and surfaces status/elevation conflicts instead of silently overriding official status.
Replaces park-wide status with entrance-to-destination route presets, projected seasonal segment checks, published delay context and an explicit final live-map check.
Separates Paradise, Sunrise, White River, Mowich and Cayuse approach decisions.
Treats Tioga as an east-west itinerary crossing and surfaces the current road note/delay context.
Prioritizes current ramp candidates instead of presenting an undifferentiated status table.

fieldTestProtocol.comparison: Same realistic trip decision completed with normal Google/official-source workflow versus the Chris Izworski decision tool.

acceptanceGate.speed: At least 30% lower median time to a correct decision than the normal Google/official-source workflow.
acceptanceGate.comprehension: At least 80% of testers can identify the main condition that would change the answer.

fieldTestProtocol.rule: Do not award a new benchmark score from implementation intent alone. Re-score after rendered mobile verification and field-test evidence.

changesRequiredByThisAudit: Put the trip consequence directly under the live result.
Expose what can flip the answer so a live result is not mistaken for certainty.
Give a concrete pre-departure checklist rather than generic source prose.
Prioritize Lake Powell ramp candidates from the current threshold/status table.
Treat Yellowstone and Mount Rainier as route/area checks, not park-wide all-clear tools.
Stop labeling the public portfolio as ten breakout bets until individual tools clear the benchmark.
